REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - AUGUST 11, 2016 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
COUNCIL CHAMBERS, BLOOMFIELD AVENUE AT 183RD STREET
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

minutes_text:
MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
AUGUST 11, 2016, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Councilmember Jim Edwards.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by “The Cyclones” Youth Soccer Team.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Carol Chen
  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Naresh Solanki
  Mayor/Chair George Ray

5.  Presentations/Appointments

  Alex Lingad, Team Manager for BLINDSTART, presented a bronze medal to
  Councilmember Chen and Mayor Pro Tem Solanki for their finish in the VIP Division Race
  in the 2016 Long Beach Dragon Festival paddle competition.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Dorothy Owen, President 1st CEB Adoption Committee, spoke regarding their
  recent award from the American Red Cross. She distributed the event brochure
  to the City Council.

  Greg Cates, representing Solar City, expressed concerns regarding a Municipal
  Code provision and solar panel installations in the City.

7.  Consent Calendar
  Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by
  one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a
  Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item will be
  removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.

7A.  Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated August 11, 2016
  (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the Register
  of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated August 11, 2016 in the total amount of
  $9,719,790.74 (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  August 11, 2016
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 2 of 5

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7B.  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of July 28,
  2016 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of July 28, 2016
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Approval of the Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending June 30, 2016
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the
  Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending June 30, 2016 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR
  AGENCY). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and introduce AN
  ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS AMENDING CHAPTER 20.30 AND
  CHAPTER 22.40 OF THE CERRITOS MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO THE
  REGULATION OF BOARDING HOUSES WITHIN THE CITY OF CERRITOS, HEREIN
  REFERENCED AS DEVELOPMENT CODE AMENDMENT 2016-4 (COUNCIL).*

  *Pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) of the California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA), this project is categorically exempt from CEQA Review.

  A staff report was given by Kristin Aguila, Advance Planning Manager. A PowerPoint
  Presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments. Noting there were no
  individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed public comments and the public
  hearing.

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Chen, to:

  1. Approve Development Code Amendment 2016-4, making the findings set forth in
  Cerritos Planning Commission Resolution No. 2016-20; and
  2. Waive full reading of and introduce Ordinance No. 1006, AN ORDINANCE OF
  THE CITY OF CERRITOS AMENDING CHAPTER 20.30 AND CHAPTER
  22.40 OF THE CERRITOS MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO THE
  REGULATION OF BOARDING HOUSES WITHIN THE CITY OF CERRITOS,
  HEREIN REFERENCED AS DEVELOPMENT CODE AMENDMENT 2016-4, as
  amended to read as follows:

  (continued on next page)
 City of Cerritos  August 11, 2016
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 3 of 5

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8A.  (continued)

  Section 20.30.137 is hereby added to Chapter 20.30 of the Cerritos
  Municipal Code to read as follows:

  “Boarding house” means an owner-occupied, single-family residential
  dwelling, including any guesthouses, second units, and other accessory
  structures, wherein one or more rooms, with or without individual or group
  cooking facilities, are rented, licensed or otherwise provided in exchange
  for rent or other remuneration to an individual or individuals under
  separate written or oral rental leases, licenses or other agreements (“rental
  agreement”) for a term of thirty consecutive calendar days or more
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of signage placement at Cerritos Recreation facilities
  prohibiting the feeding of wildlife (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Sherre Titus, Recreation Services Superintendent.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Pulido, to direct staff to erect
  signs prohibiting the feeding of waterfowl and other wildlife at Cerritos Recreation
  facilities (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration of a contract between the City of Cerritos and the
  Western Area Power Administration (WAPA) for electric services and an agreement
  with WAPA, the Bureau of Reclamation and Boulder Canyon Project Electric
  Service Contractors for energy purchases (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Vince Brar, Senior Assistant City Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  A motion made by Chen, and seconded by Solanki, to table this item until after the
  upcoming budget discussion did not pass (2 – 3, Edwards, Pulido, Ray “no”).
 City of Cerritos  August 11, 2016
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 4 of 5

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9B.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to:

  1. Authorize the City Manager to approve and execute Contract No. 16-DSR-12642
  negotiated between the City of Cerritos and WAPA for electric services; and
  2. Authorize the City Manager to approve and execute the Amended and Restated
  Implementation Agreement negotiated between WAPA, the Bureau of Reclamation
  and Boulder Canyon Project Electric Service Contractors for energy purchases.
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (3 – 2) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Ray
  NOES:  Chen, Solanki
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9C.  Review and consideration of award of a contract for construction of Liberty Park
  Annex Exterior Improvements, Project No. 10805, Bid No. 1253-17 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kanna Vancheswaran, Director of Public Works.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to:

  1. Award a contract in the amount of $237,780.00 for Liberty Park Annex Exterior
  Improvements, Project No. 10805, Bid No. 1253-17, to Sully-Miller Contracting and
  reject all other bids;
  2. Authorize staff to negotiate with Sully-Miller Contracting for additional exterior
  improvements to the Liberty Park Annex with available budgeted funds; and
  3. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any project-related change
  orders (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  August 11, 2016
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 5 of 5

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9D.  Review and consideration of a license agreement authorizing ES Engineering, Inc.
  to install and transfer ownership of a groundwater treatment system to the City
  (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Mike O’Grady, Environmental Services Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Chen, and seconded by Solanki, to authorize the City
  Manager to execute the License Agreement with ES Engineering for the Groundwater
  Treatment System Pilot Demonstration at the City of Cerritos Civic Center Parking
  Structure (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or
  Federal Legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.

  None.

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  Reports were provided by Council/Agency Members Pulido, Edwards, and Chen,
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Solanki, and Mayor/Chair Ray.

12.  Closed Session

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting was adjourned at 8:55 p.m. in memory of Van Allen Coleman.

  s/ Vida Barone_____________________
  Vida Barone, City Clerk/Agency Secretary

/s/ George Ray_________________
George Ray, Mayor/Chair
